# Environment profile config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/environments/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.EnvironmentBlock` (ADR-093 D3) declaring one **environment profile** — an operator-authored terminal an external MCP caller may name. **A recipe kind's identity regime on a config kind's table**: the filename stem is the identity, the file declares exactly one profile, and a block label that disagrees with the stem is a hard error at load and at plan (ADR-087 D3 Amendment 5).

**The decode target is the block a recipe already declares.** `pkg/config.EnvironmentBlock` is the same struct a work-order-type recipe writes inside its own `environments {}` block, and reusing it is the ratified shape rather than an economy: a second struct carrying the same fields for the same reason is a second struct to drift. What tells the two apart is where the block sits. Nested inside a recipe it is a component of that recipe with no standing of its own and a *per-recipe-unique* name; at the top level, in this directory, it is a profile whose name is **global** — which is what a caller passes and what a role grants, and which nothing but the one-profile-per-file rule could supply.

**A caller names a profile and supplies nothing else.** No command, no arguments, no working directory, no environment. That is not a validator rule an author could forget to write: `pkg/config.EnvironmentBlock` and `pkg/config.EnvironmentConfigBlock` declare no `command`, no `args`, no `workdir` and no `address` attribute at all, so a file that tries to write one **fails to parse**, naming the attribute. The entrypoint is `config { bootstrap { startup_every = [...] } }`, which the PTY provider joins into the terminal's single long-lived command; a caller who could supply that could run an arbitrary command against an operator-chosen host directory, which is ADR-085 D1's failure mode in different clothes.

**Declaring a profile is not granting one.** Reachability is a separate RBAC resource under the ADR-060 one-model rule: `environments/<name>/attach`, granted from an ordinary `role` recipe and evaluated by the ordinary ACL engine, with the ordinary `+` / `#` wildcards. Deny-by-default — a declared profile that no role grants is reachable by nobody, and **holding the tool is not authorization to get a terminal**. No standard role grants this family; `admin` reaches it only through its existing `#`.

The two refusals — an *undeclared* profile and a *declared* profile the principal lacks the grant for — are distinct code paths, both fail closed, and neither reports the profile's existence differently from its absence: same message, same shape, same timing class. An inventory an unauthorized caller can enumerate by probing names has given away what the operator runs, so the refusal is deliberately unhelpful to the caller and fully detailed in the operator's log.

v1 accepts `type = "pty"` only, and refuses the other two providers by name rather than silently: a remote desktop is declared in `.tera/remote-desktop-endpoints/` and reached by endpoint name (ADR-085 D1), and a software shell is provisioned by the `bash` tool, which resolves its own per-holder volume (ADR-076).

`mounts` is refused and `config.cwd` is **required and absolute**. A mount label is resolved against the owning Work Order's volume bindings at dispatch, and a profile has neither a Work Order nor bindings — so the working directory is an operator-chosen host path or nothing. It is the same host path for every attach to that profile: two concurrent callers holding one profile share it, and per-caller scratch isolation is not in v1.

A profile may carry a startup-`expect` dialogue with credential references (ADR-057 D10). Over MCP that dialogue is operator-only in both directions — a caller cannot influence it and should not see its output. Read `docs/ops/environment-profiles.md` before declaring one that types a credential.

Status: **preview**.

## Example

A minimal `environments`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/environments/example-environment.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

environment "example-environment" {
  type = "pty"

  config {
    cwd = "/srv/tera/example"
  }
}
```

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |

| `endpoint` | string | no | — | — | — | Name of the operator-declared remote_desktop_endpoint to attach to. Required under type = remote-desktop, rejected elsewhere. A name only — the host, port and credential are the operator's declaration (ADR-085 D1). |
| `geometry` | string | no | — | — | — | Requested framebuffer size for a remote-desktop environment, as <width>x<height> (e.g. 1280x800). Advisory — the device decides: the size it announces (and any mid-session DesktopSize change) is the truth, and a divergence from this request is reported at attach rather than corrected. Valid only under type = remote-desktop. |
